text:
deploy-bot: Config-only deploy queued for 10:30-11:00 UTC. Change summary:
- routing policy R1: reduce max_concurrent from 120 -> 102 (≈15%)
- low-priority route timeout 8s -> 5s
- enable slim_batcher, max_batch_tokens=1024, target_batch_size=8
- prefix cache TTL 60s (was 300s)
- no model version changes (config-only)
links: https://deploy.internal/redwood/changes/2367890123

micah: ack this looks like a sensible cost-control tweak. are we pinning any model hashes for fallback?

anya: no model pins — purely routing/batching/timeouts. planning canary -> 5% for 10m then observe.

shiv: canary policy: 5% traffic to R1-v2-config for 10m, check: latency_p95, errors, median tail qps. rollback if errors + latency both spike. exact criterion below.

shiv: rollback triggers (proposal):
- errors (5xx) increase > 1.5pp absolute AND
- p95 latency increase > 200ms sustained for 5m
OR
- request saturation on node pool (queue_depth > 80%) for 3m
If any trigger, immediate abort + roll back to prior routing config.

ops-oncall: please also wire an alert: `prod.routing.r1.config.deviation` on 1m for error_rate > 1% and `prod.latency.r1.p95` spike > 200ms. I'll stub an SLO monitor.

eva: quick note — prefix cache TTL drop might increase origin load for cold keys. watch origin_rps and cache_miss_rate. If miss_rate > 12% for 10m, rollback.

micah: can we add a tiny hysteresis before rollout? e.g., start canary at 2% for 3m then 5% for 7m. Safer for the TTL change.

shiv: fine. updated plan: 2% for 3m, then 5% for 7m. If healthy, ramp to 25% for 10m then to 100% over 30m.

release-bot: Please remember to append a short release note to `#release-notes`: "Config-only: R1 routing limits -15%, low-priority timeouts shortened, slim_batcher enabled, cache TTL reduced (monitor cache miss)."

anya: deployment commands (internal):
```bash
# create rollout
curl -X POST https://deploy.internal/api/rollouts -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN' -d '{"target":"R1","change":"config","canary_steps":[{"pct":2,"duration":180},{"pct":5,"duration":420},{"pct":25,"duration":600}],"meta":"cache_ttl=60,slim_batcher=on"}'
```

shiv: watching metrics dashboard -> https://dashboards.internal/r1/2367890123

ops-oncall: ack :thumbsup: I pushed the two alerts and a synthetic to hit a representative slow key every 30s.

deploy-bot: Canary start: 2% at 10:31 UTC.

micah: ack — micah here, will monitor latency and client-side errors.

(2 minutes later)
release-bot: Canary update: error_rate=0.22% (baseline 0.18%), p95 +12ms. No trigger.

(10 minutes later)
deploy-bot: Canary progressed to 5% at 10:36 UTC.

eva: cache_miss_rate ticked from 6% -> 9% after 5% rollout, origin_rps +8%. within expected.

shiv: p95 +40ms, errors flat. continue to 25%.

deploy-bot: Ramp to 25% at 10:46 UTC.

ops-oncall: synthetic shows one slow key outlier but not widespread. queue_depth ok.

(final)
deploy-bot: Deploy completed — rolled to 100% at 11:08 UTC. No rollback triggered.

micah: nice. please add a short postmortem if any customers report regressions in next 24h.

anya: will publish the release-note + config diff to the wiki.

shiv: closing this thread. thanks all. :rocket:
